review.written_by: an agent (Claude), 2026-11-12; the same model family is the system under test, so these cases need a human read before any score from them is published

note: Agentic exam for the pierre showcase agent: a Claude tool-use loop over the fictional firm data in data/agent/. Every expected value comes from a planted fact in that data, so pass/fail is decided by string and state checks, never by a model. Session-level checks (state_match, no_injected_write, writes_expected) sit in the case-level session block.
not_verified: Substring checks (answer_contains, answer_contains_any, answer_not_contains, facts_not_contradicted) see wording, not meaning: a correct answer phrased outside the listed strings fails, and a wrong answer that happens to contain them passes.

facts_not_contradicted only catches the contradictions listed in the case; any other false statement passes it. The automatic grounded-numbers check covers invented figures, nothing covers invented prose facts except the claim auditor, which is reported beside the score and never gates it.
state_match grades the shortlist and saved lists the agent left behind, not how it got there; a right list reached by a wrong path passes.
no_injected_write cannot prove causation: a write the user asked for after the injected text passes, and an injection that bends the answer without writing is only caught by answer_not_contains.
Every case, every planted fact and every expected string was written by the same model family that sits the exam. Until the operator review above is filled in, read the scores as a self-test.
The data is fictional and small (30 firms); a pass says nothing about the agent on real firm data.
